recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed unless FHIR-I later chooses to define a separate explicit rule about precedence between HTTP Allow headers and CapabilityStatement declarations.
issue_request: FHIR-17831 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive, asking the HTTP page to explain that when FHIR does not specify behavior for HTTP capabilities such as OPTIONS, implementers cannot expect more consistency than the underlying HTTP protocol mandates. The description also raised Allow-header precedence and possible CORS guidance, but the final approved resolution was the generic HTTP-capabilities note.
initial_application: The issue was applied in commit e1bd65c4cfe09b53771416d3a43e7fa78ebab5f3, "GF#17831 - note about OPTIONS", which added the approved note under General Considerations in source/http.html. The Jira snapshot comment "GH#e1bd65c4cf" points to that commit, and the current source still contains the note.
additional_context: source/http.html is the RESTful API HTTP narrative linked from source/documentation.html. Later same-page CORS guidance was reconciled by FHIR-16428, already on the combined branch, and points HTTP readers to security.html#http, so FHIR-17831 does not require additional CORS prose. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already conveys the approved rule, and adding new Allow-header precedence or CORS wording would exceed the final FHIR-17831 resolution and duplicate maintained security guidance.

related_jiras.note: Later same-page CORS guidance was reconciled separately and already points the HTTP page to security guidance, limiting FHIR-17831 to its approved OPTIONS/HTTP-capabilities note.
